req.title: Update form GET returns 200 for author
req.statement: The system shall serve the update form at GET /<id>/update when the current user is the post's author.
triggers: update form get returns 200 for author

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /<id>/update must return HTTP 200 when the current user is the post's author. We need: (1) a positive test where the logged-in user IS the author (EP, happy path); (2) a negative test where the logged-in user is NOT the author (NEG, 403 expected); (3) a boundary test using the lowest valid post id owned by the author (BVA, id=2 owned by Rahul/user 1); (4) a negative test for a non-existent post id (NEG, 404 expected); (5) a state-transition test verifying that an unauthenticated request is redirected (STC). All tests use pre-loaded data: user Rahul (id=1, password='stone') owns posts 2,3,6,8,9,10,11,12,15,18,19,20; user James (id=5, password='river') owns posts 1,4,5,16. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (200 vs 302/403/404), exact redirect location strings, both sides of the author-check branch.

tests.name: test_update_form_get_200_for_author
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
User Rahul (id=1) is the author of post id=2
User is logged in as Rahul
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_200_for_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_update_form_get_200_for_author()
